messages:
maya: FYI — Sales flagged a customer on Dedicated whose traffic overflowed and hit a hosted model variant. They want confirmation that no tenant data crossed boundaries. Need quick plan.

ryan: Do we currently emit a 'fallback' metric with tenant context? I can add one if not.

oliver: We have routing.logs but they only show pool id, not tenant. Adding tenant id there is PII risk. Suggest hashed_tenant + env tag.

tara: Customer reported subtle behavior diffs (7b -> 7b-q4). They're worried about prompt fidelity and potential information mixing.

ash: Variant differences are expected. From a model standpoint there's no state carryover, but a hosted fallback could return different outputs. Not a data leak per se but it violates their expectations.

eva: Legal: for contracts with explicit 'no-hosted-fallback' clauses, routing to hosted is a contract violation even if transient. We need audit trails + automated prevents.

maya: Proposal: tenant-level flag in Console: "allow hosted fallback". Tri-state: allow / deny / simulate. Show prominent warning for deny. Record consent for allow.

ryan: Implementation sketch: routing order = [dedicated_pool, regional_reserve, hosted]. Add policy field: hosted_fallback: { allow: false, variants: ["model-7b-q4"], audit: true }. Tri-state seems sensible.

oliver: Also need runtime checks — policy cache on nodes. If tenant policy == deny -> runtime should 429/queue rather than spillover. Where to implement?

ash: Runtime path must be fast. Control-plane owns policy but runtime must enforce a short-circuit. We can do a cached policy lookup in hot path.

ryan: Pseudoconfig (WIP):
```yaml
routing:
  order: [dedicated, regional_reserve, hosted]
  hosted_fallback:
    allow: deny
    variants_allowed: [model-7b-q4]
    audit: true
    simulate: false
```
Would like feedback on default (deny for enterprise).

tara: Alerts/SLOs: fallback_rate < 0.1% for dedicated customers. If breached -> page oncall + notify account team. Also add metric for 'fallback_decisions' with reason tag.

oliver: Infrastructure idea: per-tenant token bucket for fallback traffic (default 5 rps). Prevents one tenant from flooding hosted pool and preserves burst fairness.

ash: Edge case — prefix caching: maybe we allow cache hits to be served from hosted cache but never send full request to hosted for restricted tenants. But KV cache may leak prompt prefixes. Not acceptable for strict privacy tenants.

eva: Telemetry/data governance: any events that include tenant identifiers must go to a secure telemetry project with RBAC. No raw prompts. Use hashed_tenant and only ops+legal access.

ryan: Telemetry plan: emit metrics: routing.fallback.rate, routing.fallback.variant, routing.fallback.duration. Emit event stream 'fallback_decision' (hashed_tenant, reason, dest_model, policy_snapshot).

maya: UX notes: Console should expose tenant policy, last 24h fallback count, last_fallback_ts, and a link to SLA text. Add an inline confirmation when flipping allow -> records consent (timestamp + actor).

tara: +1 for a dry-run/simulate mode: logs decisions but doesn't reroute. Useful to estimate impact. Sales can run with customers.

oliver: Canary concern: deploy-bot is rolling v3.4.1 routing canary to cluster-a (10%). Ensure canary honors tenant policies. If we accidentally enable fallback in canary, can violate contracts.

deploy-bot: deploy:service-routing v3.4.1 started canary on cluster-a (10% traffic).

ryan: I'll enforce policy precedence: control-plane policy wins. Runtime will check cached policy and if missing default to denial for enterprise-tenants. I'll open a PR for schema + telemetry.

oliver: Infra will add token-bucket limit + secure telemetry project. Also will review storage of policy snapshots for audit (signed, append-only).

ash: Runtime change: fast-path policy check + 429 behavior for deny. For simulate mode, emit event but do not reroute.

eva: Legal will implement a contract-monitor: when account is marked 'no-hosted-fallback' and we detect a policy flip or an actual fallback event, automated email to legal + account team.

maya: Rollout plan: 1) implement schema & telemetry (ryan) 2) infra token-buckets & audit store (oliver) 3) runtime short-circuit + simulate (ash) 4) console tri-state + consent UI (maya) 5) alerts/SLOs (tara) 6) legal hooks (eva). Start internal opt-in for 2 weeks, then default deny for new enterprise customers.

ryan: Assigning myself for PR, pinging oliver for infra review.

oliver: We'll target a canary that explicitly runs in 'simulate' mode first, then enable enforcement after 2 weeks.

maya: Great. I'll sync with Sales and CS to prepare customer comms and update the SLA page. Weekly check-in on Friday.

deploy-bot: deploy:service-routing v3.4.1 canary paused (awaiting policy rollback test).

tara: One more ask — can we add a dashboard card: 'Dedicated -> Hosted fallback heatmap by region' and a table for tenants with >0 fallbacks in last 7d. That helps CS triage.

ryan: Will add dashboard tiles to Console: fallback_rate, last_7d_tenants, variant_distribution.

maya: Thanks everyone. Filing action items in GH and emailing sales.
